授業科目の概要.科目名称: Japan in Globalization: A Sociological Perspective
授業科目の概要.講義題目: Japan in Globalization: A Sociological Perspective
授業科目の概要.授業科目に関する特筆事項: This is an ‘all-English’ course – all the class-related activities, including lectures, class discussions, readings, and required homework, will be carried out using English as the medium of communication.

授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）:
現代日本はグローバリゼーションの産物であると同時にそれを推進する力の一部でもある。
この科目は「グローバリゼーションの社会学」の概論として、現代日本社会が直面している多様な課題とその展望を近年のグローバリゼーションとの関連性のうえで議論していく。これらの課題が、どのようにグローバリゼーションによりもたらされまた国際社会へ波及しているかを、社会学的観点から理解を深めていく。
この科目では、主にグローバリゼーションの歴史的変容、移民をめぐる諸問題、犯罪の国際化、メディアや教育などの社会基盤の変容、環境問題、「性」の多様性、またポップカルチャーの役割などに着目する。
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）:
Globalization refers to a set of ongoing processes that continually shape and reshape individuals’ lives in society. Japan, as we know it today, is both a contributor to and a product of globalization. This course serves as an introduction to the sociology of globalization, exploring significant sociological issues and challenges that contemporary Japanese society faces in relation to modern globalization. The primary objective of this course is to understand the interplay between Japan and globalization by examining how contemporary issues, trends, and challenges in Japanese society both contribute to and are influenced by globalization.
Topics of discussion will include, but are not limited to, the historical stages of globalization, transnational migration, the globalization of crime, the evolving roles of mass media and education, environmental changes, transformations in sexuality, demographic shifts, and popular culture.
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.キーワード: Japan, Globalization, Social Problems, Social Changes, Sociology
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.履修条件:
This course does not have any prerequisites. However, please note the following:
This course is designed to promote international and cross-cultural co-learning between international and Japanese students at Kyushu University. To facilitate this, all activities and materials—including lectures, discussions, and reading materials—will be provided in English.
While students are not formally required to have a specific level of English proficiency to enroll in this course, it is strongly recommended that non-native English speakers possess the minimum English skills necessary for meaningful participation, effective learning, and successful completion of the course. For reference, a TOEFL score of 79 (IBT) or an IELTS score of 6.0 is recommended.
